value.rationale: The Thomas system is defined by a directed three-edge nonlinear feedback ring, and the literature emphasizes that a single damping parameter produces equilibria, cycles, multiple coexisting attractors, and chaos. The accepted theorem gives that architecture an exact stationary statistical meaning: on every receiving-coordinate fiber, the incoming sine feedback is calibrated exactly to damping, even when the invariant state itself is not cyclically symmetric. The resulting variance defects identify mean-square coordinate speed as the exact loss in feedback coherence, and the one-Lipschitz property closes the three local identities into a quantitative global speed budget. These laws provide exact, componentwise consistency checks for periodic or chaotic invariant measures in a system where numerical standard deviations and coexisting attractors are already central observables.
